card.statement: A set $\mathcal N$ of subsets of a set $S$ is called a filter on $S$ if $S\in \mathcal N$, $\emptyset\not\in \mathcal N$, the intersection of two elements of $\mathcal N$ is again in $\mathcal  N$, and any subset of $S$ containing a set in $\mathcal N$ is again in $\mathcal N$. Suppose $\mathcal B$ is a collection of subsets of a given set $S$ and consider the set $\mathcal N=\{F\subseteq  S\,|\, \exists B\in  \mathcal B,B\subseteq F\}$. If $\mathcal N$ is a filter on $S$, then $\mathcal B$ is called a filter base on $S$. A fundamental system of neighborhoods of zero in a vector space is any filter base generating the neighborhoods of zero.
card.label: Definition 11

paper.title: Virasoro action on Imaginary Verma modules and the operator form of the KZ-equation
paper.abstract: We define the Virasoro algebra action on imaginary Verma modules for affine sl(2) and construct the analogs of Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equation in the operator form. Both these results are based on a free field realization of imaginary Verma modules.
